summary.en: TELUS Ventures (TELUS Global Ventures), founded in 2001 and based in Vancouver, is the corporate venture arm of telecom TELUS. It is among Canada's most active and longest-standing CVCs, with ~$500M AUM and a $625M fund, investing $500K–$15M from seed to growth in digital health, agtech, IoT, AI and security companies. It has invested in 100+ companies since inception.

strategy.thesis: A $100M corporate social impact fund operated by TELUS investing in for-profit companies generating both financial and social returns across climate/clean technology, healthcare, responsible agriculture and inclusive communities, pairing capital with TELUS's distribution, data and technical assets.

summary.en: Launched in 2020 by telecom TELUS, the $100M Pollinator Fund for Good is one of the world's largest corporate social impact funds. It makes Seed and Series A investments in for-profit companies tackling climate/cleantech, healthcare, responsible agriculture and inclusion, leveraging TELUS's non-financial assets. By its second impact report it had deployed nearly $40M across 26 startups.

summary.en: Shopify Ventures, founded in 2020 and based in Ottawa, is the corporate venture arm of e-commerce platform Shopify. strategy.thesis: Corporate venture arm of Thomson Reuters investing primarily at Series A in early-stage technology companies across legal tech, tax & accounting, fintech, risk/fraud/compliance and news & media — markets adjacent to Thomson Reuters' own businesses.

summary.en: Thomson Reuters Ventures, launched in 2021 and based in Toronto, is the corporate venture arm of information/technology company Thomson Reuters. Its first fund was US$100M (2021) and its second, launched 2025, is US$150M (CAD$215M), bringing total commitment to US$250M. It targets Series A deals of US$4–7M in legal, tax, fintech, risk/compliance and media tech, with 23 Fund 1 investments including Materia (acquired 2024).

strategy.thesis: Originally OpenText's corporate venture fund (OpenText was the sole 'industrial' LP alongside financial LPs), investing in Canadian B2B enterprise software companies past initial commercialization. Now operates as independent firm First Ascent Ventures.

summary.en: Founded in 2014 as the OpenText Enterprise Apps Fund (OTEAF) — a $100M Canadian B2B enterprise-software fund in which OpenText was the sole 'industrial' LP alongside financial LPs — it invested $2–10M from Series A onward in commercialized enterprise software. It subsequently rebranded to First Ascent Ventures and closed a $125M Fund II in 2021, now operating as an independent VC rather than a pure OpenText corporate vehicle.

strategy.thesis: Corporate venture arm of toy and entertainment company Spin Master, making strategic minority investments to accelerate growth across its three creative centres — toys, entertainment and digital games — focused on emerging technologies and pioneering services in the kids' space.

summary.en: Spin Master Ventures is the $100M corporate venture arm of Toronto-based toy and entertainment company Spin Master, established in 2021. It makes strategic minority investments to accelerate growth across toys, entertainment and digital games, focusing on emerging technologies and services in the kids' space, with a global geographic focus. Initial investments included game studio Nørdlight and online tutoring service Hoot Reading.

strategy.thesis: Former corporate venture arm of Rogers Communications (sole LP), investing in early-stage breakthrough technology companies — telecommunications services, products and software (web/mobile marketplaces, SaaS).

summary.en: Rogers Venture Partners was the corporate venture arm of Canadian telecom Rogers Communications, established in 2012 as a $150M fund headquartered in Palo Alto with Rogers as sole LP. It invested in early-stage technology companies (telecom, SaaS, web/mobile marketplaces) and built a portfolio of ~41 companies. It is now permanently closed; its last recorded investment was in 2018 (ScribbleLive).
